WHAT IS BEING PROVED. R1262 made every cargo command a Rust program issues

injections.name: a-cargo-spawn-goes-round-the-door
injections.why: this is the shape the law was written for: a `Command::new` naming cargo is a site with no declaration for any law to read, and every cargo spawn in this repository was one until R1262

injections.name: the-declaration-is-a-value-nobody-can-read
injections.why: a `Tree` decided at runtime is a declaration in name only — the reader cannot say which arm it is, and reporting it as declared would put a command over an unknown workspace into the judged population

injections.name: the-walk-stops-reading-rust-at-all
injections.why: an empty population holds every command it found to the law, which is also what a walk that read nothing does — and the direction it fails in reads as a clean repository

injections.name: a-bare-name-is-resolved-through-a-function-of-that-name
injections.why: the first draft's own defect, and the reason the door needs no excuse: `Command::new(program)` inside a function TAKING `program` resolved through `fn program()` in the same file, so the one site that IS the door read as a second one. Both halves are asserted — the door leaves the unplaceable pile and arrives in the finding list

injections.name: the-spelling-cargo-checks-stops-being-read
injections.why: `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_…")` names most of the spawns in this repository, and losing it moves a hundred sites into the pile this law says nothing about — WITHOUT any of them becoming a second door, so the finding list stays empty while the reader has gone blind. That is why the placed spawns have a floor of their own
